question:
Match the (List-I - Geographical regions) with (List II - Reason for their distinct climate) and select your answer the code below: List I  (geographical
regions) List II (reason for their distinct climate) (a) Rajasthan (i) Houses have sloping roofs (b) Tarai region (ii) Houses have thick walls and flat roofs (c) Assam (iii) Houses are built on stilts (d) Goa (iv) Experiences seasonal rain during October and November (RPF SI CBT-I 2024 (12/12/2024) Shift 2)
options: a - iv, b - iii, c - ii, d - i
a - iii, b - i, c - ii, d - iv
a - ii, b - i, c - iii, d - iv
a - iii, b - ii, c - i, d - iv
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is a - ii, b - i, c - iii, d - iv

Explanation:
Rajasthan has a hot and dry climate, so houses have thick walls and flat roofs to protect from heat. The Tarai region experiences heavy rainfall and marshy conditions, leading to houses built on stilts to avoid dampness and floods. Assam receives very high rainfall, hence houses have sloping roofs to drain water quickly. Goa experiences seasonal rain during October and November due to the retreating monsoon (northeast monsoon). These architectural adaptations reflect the distinct climatic conditions of each region.

☛ Tarai region characteristic → Marshy land, high rainfall
☛ Climate of Assam → Tropical monsoon, very high rainfall

☛ Region with thick walls and flat roofs → Rajasthan

question: Which of the following periods was considered as the second phase of the Green Revolution in India? (RPF SI CBT-I 2024 (12/12/2024) Shift 3)
options: Mid-1960s to mid-1970s
1960s to 1970s
Mid-1970s to mid-1980s
1970s to 1980s
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Mid-1970s to mid-1980s

Explanation:
The Green Revolution in India took place in two phases. The first phase lasted from the mid-1960s to the mid-1970s, introducing high-yielding varieties of wheat and rice. The second phase, from the mid-1970s to the mid-1980s, focused on the extensive use of fertilizers, pesticides, and irrigation. This phase further increased agricultural productivity and helped India achieve food grain self-sufficiency. It also expanded to include crops like oilseeds and pulses.

question: In reference to air transport of India, what is the full form of AERA?  (RPF SI CBT-I 2024 (12/12/2024) Shift 3)
options: Airports Economic Regulatory Authority of India
Aviation Equipment Regulatory Authority
Aircraft Electronic-warfare Retractor Appratus
Aviation Economic Regulatory Authority of India
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Airports Economic Regulatory Authority of India

Explanation:
AERA stands for Airports Economic Regulatory Authority of India. It is a statutory body established under the AERA Act of 2008. Its primary function is the economic regulation of airports, including determining aerodrome charges and tariffs for services. It sets the maximum charges for major airports like Delhi and Mumbai and monitors the operations of private airports. AERA's headquarters is located in New Delhi. The authority ensures fair pricing and promotes efficiency in the airport sector.

☛ What is the main function of AERA? → Economic regulation of airports

question: Which of the following winds govern the climate of India during winter? (RPF SI CBT-I 2024 (12/12/2024) Shift 3)
options: Westerlies
Southwest monsoon winds
Northeast monsoon winds
Northeast trade winds
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Northeast trade winds

Explanation:
The winds that govern the climate of India during winter are the northeast trade winds. These winds blow from the high-pressure area in the northern hemisphere towards the equator. In winter, when the sun is active in the southern hemisphere, Asia experiences cold and dry weather. During this time, the northeast trade winds blow from the cold regions of the Himalayas and Central Asia towards India, bringing dry and cold air. These winds cause clear skies and low rainfall over most parts of India during winter. The southwest monsoon brings rain in summer, while westerlies are active in mid-latitudes. Understanding the seasonal wind patterns is crucial for studying Indian climate.

Important one-liners for upcoming exams:

☛ Direction of northeast trade winds → Northeast to southwest
☛ Nature of these winds in winter → Dry and cold
☛ Winds bringing summer rainfall → Southwest monsoon
☛ Trade winds blow from → Subtropical high to equator
question_hi: निम्नलिखित में से कौन सी पवनें भारत की जलवायु को सर्दियों के दौरान नियंत्रित करती हैं? (RPF SI CBT-I 2024 (12/12/2024) Shift 3)

उत्तर-पूर्व मानसून पवनें

solution_hi:
Solution: सही उत्तर है उत्तर-पूर्व व्यापारिक पवनें

Explanation:
भारत में सर्दियों के दौरान जलवायु को नियंत्रित करने वाली प्रमुख पवनें उत्तर-पूर्व व्यापारिक पवनें हैं। ये पवनें उत्तरी गोलार्ध में उच्च दबाव क्षेत्र से भूमध्य रेखा की ओर बहती हैं। सर्दियों में, जब सूर्य दक्षिणी गोलार्ध में सक्रिय होता है, तब एशिया में ठंडा और शुष्क मौसम होता है। इस समय उत्तर-पूर्व व्यापारिक पवनें हिमालय और मध्य एशिया के ठंडे क्षेत्रों से होकर भारत की ओर बहती हैं, जो शुष्क और ठंडी होती हैं। ये पवनें भारत के अधिकांश भागों में सर्दियों के दौरान स्पष्ट आकाश और कम वर्षा का कारण बनती हैं। दक्षिण-पश्चिम मानसून गर्मियों में वर्षा लाता है, जबकि पश्चिमी पवनें मध्य अक्षांशों में सक्रिय रहती हैं।

question: The Ganga-Brahmaputra-Meghna system is composed of which of the following main sub-basins? (RPF SI CBT-I 2024 (12/12/2024) Shift 3)
options: Bhagirathi and Alaknanda
Alaknanda and Gandak
Bhagirathi and Yamuna
Yamuna and Ramganga
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Bhagirathi and Alaknanda

Explanation:
The Ganga-Brahmaputra-Meghna system is one of the largest delta regions in the world. This system is primarily composed of three sub-basins: the Ganga, the Brahmaputra, and the Meghna. The Ganga river originates from the Gangotri Glacier in the Himalayas, where it is known as the Bhagirathi. At Prayagraj (Allahabad), the Bhagirathi and Alaknanda rivers converge to form the Ganga. These two streams are the main headwaters of the Ganga and are considered its principal sub-basins. Other options like Alaknanda and Gandak or Bhagirathi and Yamuna are incorrect because the Yamuna joins later and Gandak is a separate tributary. Therefore, the Bhagirathi and Alaknanda are the main sub-basins of the Ganga-Brahmaputra-Meghna system.

Important one-liners for upcoming exams:
☛ Ganga-Brahmaputra-Meghna system → Three main sub-basins: Ganga, Brahmaputra, Meghna
☛ Origin of Ganga → Gangotri Glacier (as Bhagirathi)
☛ Confluence of Bhagirathi and Alaknanda → Prayagraj (Devprayag)
☛ Major tributary of Ganga → Yamuna (confluence at Prayagraj)
☛ Origin of Brahmaputra → In Tibet as the Tsangpo River
question_hi: गंगा-ब्रह्मपुत्र-मेघना तंत्र निम्नलिखित में से किस मुख्य उप-बेसिन से बना है? (RPF SI CBT-I 2024 (12/12/2024) Shift 3)

question: Which of the following states has benefited from the ‘Sirhind’ canal? (RPF SI CBT-I 2024 (12/12/2024) Shift 3)
options: Bihar
Uttar Pradesh
Punjab
West Benga
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Punjab

Explanation:
The Sirhind canal is a major canal in northern India located in the state of Punjab. It was constructed by the British in 1882 and originates from the Ropar headworks on the Sutlej river. This canal provides irrigation facilities to several districts of Punjab such as Rupnagar, Fatehgarh Sahib, Patiala, Sangrur, Ludhiana, and Moga. Due to the Sirhind canal, Punjab has greatly benefited in agricultural production and it plays a significant role in the state's economy. This canal does not benefit any other state besides Punjab. Bihar, Uttar Pradesh, and West Bengal do not receive any irrigation facilities from the Sirhind canal.

☛ What type of canal is the Sirhind canal? → Irrigation canal

question: During which of the following seasons do the Southwest Monsoon winds enter the Indian Peninsula? (RPF SI CBT-I 2024 (12/12/2024) Shift 3)
options: Summer
Post-Monsoon
Winter
Rainy Season
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Rainy Season

Explanation:
The Southwest Monsoon winds enter the Indian Peninsula between June and September, which is known as the Rainy Season. This monsoon brings moisture from the Indian Ocean and accounts for most of India's annual rainfall. The monsoon first arrives at the Kerala coast. Summer (March-May) is characterized by high temperatures without rainfall. Post-Monsoon (October-November) sees reduced rainfall. Winter (December-February) experiences the Northeast Monsoon. The Southwest Monsoon is crucial for agriculture in India.

question: Which of the following is NOT a tributary of the Godavari river? (RPF SI CBT-I 2024 (13/12/2024) Shift 1)

question: In which of the following types of vegetation would we find species like ebony, mahogany, and rosewood? (RPF SI CBT-I 2024 (13/12/2024) Shift 1)
options: Tropical deciduous forests
Montane forests
Tropical evergreen forests
Mangrove forests
solution:

Explanation:
Species like ebony, mahogany, and rosewood are found in Tropical evergreen forests. These forests are located near the equator, where rainfall and temperature remain high throughout the year. question: On which river system is the National Waterway 1, developed by the Indian government, built? (RPF SI CBT-I 2024 (13/12/2024) Shift 1)

Stretches of Godavari and Krishna rivers
solution:

Explanation:
National Waterway 1 (NW-1) is India's longest national waterway, developed on the Ganges-Bhagirathi-Hooghly river system stretching from Haldia (West Bengal) to Allahabad (Uttar Pradesh). It has a total length of approximately 1,620 km. This waterway passes through Uttar Pradesh, Bihar, Jharkhand, and West Bengal, and is used for cargo and passenger transportation. The Inland Waterways Authority of India (IWAI) is responsible for its development and management. Various hydroelectric projects and multi-purpose river valley projects are also being implemented on NW-1.

question: The annual precipitation in Meghalaya exceeds 400 cm, while in Ladakh and western Rajasthan, it is less than 10 cm. Based on the statement, which of the following is the pattern of annual precipitation in India? (RPF SI CBT-I 2024 (13/12/2024) Shift 2)

Highly variable, with significant differences between regions
Uniform across the country
More in the western parts
solution:

Explanation:
India's annual precipitation distribution is highly variable. Meghalaya receives over 400 cm annually, while Ladakh and western Rajasthan get less than 10 cm. This is due to geographical diversity, monsoonal winds, and mountain ranges. Cherrapunji and Mawsynram in Meghalaya are among the wettest places on Earth. Conversely, the Thar Desert receives minimal rainfall. This variation depends on the monsoonal branches from the Bay of Bengal and Arabian Sea. Thus, rainfall is not uniform but widely differs regionally.

question: Which of the following river systems is characterised by fixed course, absence of meanders, and non-perennial flow? (RPF SI CBT-I 2024 (13/12/2024) Shift 2)
options: Ganga
Brahmaputra
Peninsular
Himalayan
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Peninsular

Explanation:
The Peninsular river system is characterized by a fixed course, absence of meanders, and non-perennial flow. These rivers flow in the Peninsular India, originating from the Western Ghats or the central Indian hills. They mostly drain into the Bay of Bengal, with the exception of Narmada and Tapi which flow westwards into the Arabian Sea. Their flow is dependent on rainfall, making them non-perennial. Unlike Himalayan rivers, they do not form meanders due to the hard rock terrain and have a relatively straight and fixed course. Major peninsular rivers include Godavari, Krishna, Kaveri, Mahanadi, Narmada, and Tapi. The hard crystalline rocks of the peninsular shield prevent the rivers from changing their course frequently. This stability in course and the seasonal nature of flow are key distinguishing features from Himalayan rivers.

☛ Peninsular rivers flowing west → Narmada and Tapi
☛ Origin of peninsular rivers → Western Ghats and central Indian hills

☛ Characteristics of Peninsular rivers → Fixed course, no meanders, non-perennial flow

question: Which of the following types of farming is largely confined to the regions having annual rainfall less than 75 cm in India?  (RPF SI CBT-I 2024 (13/12/2024) Shift 3)
options: Wetland Farming
Dryland Farming
Plantation Agriculture
Moist Farming
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Dryland Farming

Explanation:
Dryland farming is practiced in regions where annual rainfall is less than 75 cm. In India, it is mainly confined to arid and semi-arid areas like Rajasthan, Gujarat, and the Deccan Plateau. This type of farming heavily relies on rainfall due to limited irrigation facilities. Crops like jowar, bajra, gram, and oilseeds are grown, which require less water and are drought-resistant. In contrast, wetland farming and moist farming are practiced in high rainfall areas (over 100 cm), while plantation agriculture involves large-scale commercial cultivation of cash crops like tea and coffee. Thus, dryland farming is the most suitable method for regions with less than 75 cm of annual rainfall.

question: Which of the following is the oldest landmass of India? (RPF SI CBT-I 2024 (13/12/2024) Shift 3)

question: Which of the following synthetic chemicals was responsible for the sharp drop in the amount of ozone in the atmosphere in the 1980s? (RRB Technician Grade III (10/03/2026) Shift 1)
options: Chloroiodocarbons
Iodobromocarbons
Chlorofluorocarbons
Iodofluorocarbons
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Chlorofluorocarbons

Explanation:
The sharp decline in the ozone layer during the 1980s was primarily caused by synthetic chemicals called Chlorofluorocarbons (CFCs). These compounds were widely used in refrigerators, air conditioners, and aerosol sprays. When released into the atmosphere, UV radiation breaks them down, releasing chlorine atoms that destroy ozone molecules. A single chlorine atom can destroy up to 100,000 ozone molecules. This discovery led to the Montreal Protocol in 1987, which banned the production of CFCs. Since then, the ozone layer has been gradually recovering.

question: In an aquatic ecosystem, the phenomenon of biomagnification can best be studied in the case of _________. (RRB JE ECE (22/04/2025) Shift 2 CBT 2)
options: phosphates
chlorine
organochlorine
DDT
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is DDT

Explanation:
Biomagnification refers to the increasing concentration of a toxic substance at successive trophic levels in a food chain. DDT is an organochlorine pesticide that is fat-soluble and non-biodegradable. In aquatic ecosystems, it starts from phytoplankton and moves up through fish, birds, and eventually humans. The concentration of DDT increases 10-100 times at each trophic level. This makes DDT the best example for studying biomagnification. Substances like phosphates and chlorine do not show biomagnification because they are water-soluble or transient.

वैश्विक तापमान वृद्धि के कारण पृथ्वी का औसत तापमान पिछले 100 वर्षों में लगभग 0.6°C बढ़ा है। यह वृद्धि मुख्यतः ग्रीनहाउस गैसों जैसे कार्बन डाइऑक्साइड, मीथेन और नाइट्रस ऑक्साइड के उत्सर्जन के कारण हुई है। जलवायु परिवर्तन पर अंतरसरकारी पैनल (IPCC) की रिपोर्ट के अनुसार, यह वृद्धि मानवीय गतिविधियों का परिणाम है। तापमान में यह वृद्धि ग्लेशियरों के पिघलने, समुद्र स्तर में वृद्धि और चरम मौसमी घटनाओं को जन्म दे रही है। वैश्विक तापमान वृद्धि को सीमित करने के लिए पेरिस समझौते के तहत 2°C से नीचे रखने का लक्ष्य निर्धारित किया गया है।

question: Which of the following is NOT toxic to non-target organisms in the soil? (RRB JE ECE (22/04/2025) Shift 2 CBT 2)
options: Organic fertilisers
Fungicides
Herbicides
Pesticides
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Organic fertilisers

Explanation:
Organic fertilisers are derived from natural sources like manure, compost, and plant residues. They enrich the soil with organic matter and nutrients without harming non-target organisms such as earthworms, beneficial bacteria, and other soil microbes. In contrast, fungicides, herbicides, and pesticides are chemical substances designed to kill specific pests or weeds but often have toxic effects on non-target soil organisms as well. Organic fertilisers are environmentally friendly and help maintain soil fertility and biodiversity.
